title: Acne: sebum, blocked follicles, bacteria and inflammation
ariaLabel: Schematic of acne: oil glands make sebum, the hair follicle lining sheds and blocks the follicle, Cutibacterium acnes grows in the plugged follicle, and the immune response causes inflammation. Isotretinoin lowers sebum, topical retinoids normalise follicle shedding, benzoyl peroxide and antibiotics reduce bacteria, and antibiotics and retinoids also lower inflammation.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Oil gland drive
nodes.info: Androgens drive sebaceous glands to make sebum.

nodes.label: Sebum made
nodes.info: Oil that feeds bacteria and plugs follicles.

nodes.label: Follicle shedding
nodes.info: Cells lining the follicle shed abnormally and stick together.

nodes.label: C. acnes
nodes.info: Cutibacterium acnes grows in the sebum-rich plugged follicle.

nodes.label: Immune response
nodes.info: The immune system reacts to bacteria and ruptured follicles.

nodes.label: Acne severity
nodes.info: A teaching score for acne severity.

edges.label: sebum production
edges.info: Isotretinoin shrinks sebaceous glands and sharply cuts sebum. It is teratogenic, so pregnancy must be prevented. Anti-androgen hormone treatments act here too.

edges.label: follicle plugging
edges.info: Topical retinoids (tretinoin, adapalene) normalise shedding so comedones do not form. They cause dryness and irritation and are avoided in pregnancy.

edges.label: bacterial growth
edges.info: Benzoyl peroxide kills the bacteria and does not cause resistance. Antibiotics (doxycycline, clindamycin) lower bacteria and inflammation but should be combined with benzoyl peroxide to limit resistance.

edges.label: inflammation
edges.info: Tetracycline antibiotics and retinoids also lower inflammation. Oral steroids are rarely used.

sources: Where each class acts. Isotretinoin lowers sebum, topical retinoids stop follicle plugging, benzoyl peroxide kills bacteria, and antibiotics lower bacteria and inflammation. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Hormonal treatment (oestrogen-progestin, spironolactone), azelaic acid, isotretinoin monitoring (lipids, liver, mood) and the pregnancy prevention programme, scarring, rosacea, resistance, other skin conditions and sun protection are left out. Acne severity is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
